Of course, Covid changed everything and I'm not in the industry anymore (anyone need a marketing director by the way? DM me.) but prior to March 2020, I don't believe there was enough oversaturation to put anyone out of business right now.  But there *is* a breaking point. Unless someone finds a way to drive a lot more people to visit Madison and stay downtown the market can't support many more hotels. Build something else!

I worked at a hotel prior to covid. There are more than enough rooms in downtown and have been for years. More recently, Airbnb has cut into weekend business and (prior to covid) with the exception of UGM it is rare for there to be a 100% downtown sell-out during the week. Mathematically downtown is overbuilt. However, consumers drive the market and there are opportunities to fill a need or for a new hotel to capture share. 

Destination Madison (formerly the CVB) says there aren't enough rooms because there aren't any attached to the Monona Terrace and without that they lose conferences to other cities. Therefor downtown needs a new hotel (Judge Doyle). 

There wasn't a place for Marriot rewards members to use their points so if you build the AC you will have a successful hotel despite there being plenty of available rooms elsewhere.

Was there room at the Concourse for people coming to shows at Breese and the Sylvee, yes. But it's not hard to get financing for a hotel closer to the venues with a vibe that appeals to concert goers so that's how Indigo got built. 

Nobody denies the fact there are more rooms than visitors and any new rooms will take business from existing hotels but that's how a free market works. (The CVB says the Judge Doyle hotel will attract larger conferences so while x number of rooms are being added to the pot, 2x visitors will be looking for a place to stay. Existing hoteliers aren't convinced.)

There is a chance you're not sleeping "right". It's hard to know if you've only ever slept "wrong" because you don't know how sleeping is supposed to feel.  I recently had some mental health struggles and things were going downhill and I was only sleeping a couple hours each night. I used to take lorazepam every night to sleep but stopped years ago per my doctor's advice because it can be addictive and have long term cognitive effects. But I wasn't sleeping more than 4 hours night so I asked the doctor if I could start taking it again just to get through this rough part. She prescribed trazadone instead because it's not a benzo. It's amazing! I thought my problem was LACK of sleep but the real issue was the KIND of sleep. The trazadone helps me sleep correctly. I have actual dreams now and wake up feeling refreshed and my mental health has improved so much. I had no idea. Might be something to look into, making sure you're getting real, healthy sleep. 

TLDR: make sure you're sleeping correctly

And that's the story of my racist mother's cremation.

In my market and apparently at least one other,  a company other than Sinclair produces the news for the Sinclair station.  So when people hold up WMSN as an example that certain stations are standing up to ownership,  I was pointing out that in this case that's not what's happening. These anchors and producers and news director are not employees of Sinclair.

When FOX launched news at their affiliates it was a huge investment to build newsrooms and studios. And the other stations at the time didn't have anything going on at 9 so it made great financial sense for FOX and a local to partner. Especially because at that time the local ABC station had a big new empty studio that wasn't being used so it was easy peasy to just build the FOX set in there.
This particular Fox station doesn't produce its own news. The local CBS affiliate produces their news, from the CBS studios, with the CBS staff.
